title: Ephemeral kernel packing for quantized execution paths
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Mixed-precision inference paths (INT8/FP8 hybrids) are paying a large wall-clock penalty from transient host/device casts and small intermediate buffers during streaming decode and prefill. This shows up as tail-latency spikes and token-level jitter for live chat workloads. Current approaches either (a) perform frequent cast/reconstruct steps in separate kernels which introduce device memory churn, or (b) perform coarse-grained falling back to FP16 which increases cost.

Goal: Implement an ephemeral kernel packing mechanism that at runtime composes lightweight fused microkernels which perform quantized input unpack -> compute -> re-packing (where needed) within a single GPU kernel invocation for common attention/ffn micro-paths. This reduces kernel launch overhead, avoids short-lived GPU allocations for small temporaries, and keeps KV cache access patterns contiguous for streaming prefill/decode.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end streaming decode 95th-percentile latency reduced by >=18% on INT8 mixed-precision workloads (measured on c6g-like GPUTYPE in our infra)
No regression (>2%) in output accuracy vs baseline quantized path for evaluation prompt set (per quality harness)
Feature guarded by runtime flag `ephemeral_kernel_packing` and gated by model/arch whitelist
Automated microbenchmarks added to CI for per-kernel latency and memory-alloc counts
Can roll back to existing kernel set with zero state migration during rollout
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - design (2w): define microkernel ABI for packed execution, register/lookup semantics, and packing templates for attention+kv-access and fused-ffn blocks
Phase 2 - prototype (3w): implement prototype fused kernel for attention prefill path (short sequence lengths) and a small microkernel generator that emits the packed dispatch wrapper
Phase 3 - integration (2w): integrate selector into kernel arbiter, add model whitelist, expose runtime feature flag and SDK telemetry hooks
Phase 4 - benchmarking & safety (1w): run large-scale A/B tests, validate accuracy, add observability metrics and fallback thresholds
Phase 5 - rollout (gradual): canary on dedicated pools, then default-on for eligible models after 2-week stability window
benchmarks: Microbench: single-token decode (batch=1) on test-gpu-04: baseline INT8 path median=6.3ms p95=12.8ms -> ephemeral packed median=5.1ms p95=10.2ms
Full workload: chat-load-42 on canary pool (1k users): token-throughput +11%, compute utilization +7%, GPU free-memory churn reduced by 32%
Quality: eval-set-2026-01: token-level edit-rate difference vs quant baseline <0.5%
rollout_plan: Start: deploy to canary shard (5% traffic) with telemetry probes for latency, error rates, and quality regressions
Monitor: 48-hour stability criteria (no >5% p95 regression, no new OOMs), if failures auto-disable via feature flag
Fallback: runtime arbiter will fallback model->fp16 path if ephemeral kernel returns UNHANDLED or OOM
Postmortem: if enabled flagged off, capture trace+micro-kernel logs for debugging
risks_and_mitigations: Increased binary/codegen complexity: keep microkernel generator small and well-tested; add fuzz tests for combinatorial packing templates
Model coverage gaps: maintain a whitelist and graceful fallback; run model corpus offline to expand coverage
Unexpected memory patterns leading to OOMs: add preflight allocation checks and fail open to fallback path
Telemetry blind spots: emit per-request kernel variant id and memory-alloc counter; run nightly drift detection
